riskClassification.metaDescription: EU AI Act four-tier risk classification with guided Annex III wizard.
riskClassification.title: Risk Classification
riskClassification.intro: Classify your AI systems using the EU AI Act four-tier risk framework. The guided wizard walks you through Annex III categories to determine the correct risk level, with full classification history for audit purposes.
riskClassification.tiersIntro: The EU AI Act defines four risk levels. Each level carries different compliance obligations, from outright prohibition to minimal transparency requirements.

unacceptable.description: AI systems that pose an unacceptable risk to safety or fundamental rights. These are prohibited under Art. 5.
unacceptable.examples: Social scoring, real-time biometric identification in public spaces, manipulation techniques.

high.description: AI systems listed in Annex III or used as safety components. Subject to full compliance requirements (Art. 6-51).
high.examples: Biometric identification, critical infrastructure, employment decisions, law enforcement.

limited.description: AI systems with specific transparency obligations. Users must be informed they are interacting with AI (Art. 50).
limited.examples: Chatbots, deepfake generators, emotion recognition systems.

minimal.description: AI systems posing minimal risk. No mandatory compliance requirements, though voluntary codes of conduct are encouraged.
minimal.examples: Spam filters, AI-enabled video games, inventory management systems.

riskClassification.annexIntro: The classification wizard guides you through the Annex III high-risk categories. If your AI system falls into any of these areas, it is likely classified as High Risk.
riskClassification.historyIntro: Every classification change is versioned with a timestamp, the author, the previous and new risk levels, and a rationale. This provides a complete audit trail for regulators.

historyEntries.author: Maria G.
historyEntries.note: Initial classification based on chatbot use case.

historyEntries.author: Jan K.
historyEntries.note: Re-classified after scope change to include employment screening.

riskClassification.howToTitle: How to Classify an AI System

steps.title: Open the AI system
steps.description: Navigate to the AI Registry and select the system you want to classify.

steps.title: Start the classification wizard
steps.description: Go to AI Systems → Risk Classification and click Classify to launch the guided wizard.

steps.title: Answer the Annex III questions
steps.description: The wizard asks whether your system falls into any high-risk category. Answer honestly — the result determines compliance obligations.

steps.title: Review the suggested risk level
steps.description: Based on your answers, the system suggests a risk tier. You can accept or override with justification.

steps.title: Document the rationale
steps.description: Add a rationale explaining the classification decision. This is stored in the classification history for audit purposes.

assessments.title: Assessments
assessments.intro: Conduct AI-specific impact assessments using configurable templates. Score risks, document mitigations, and manage approval workflows for FRIA, conformity, AI risk, and bias/fairness assessments.

fria.label: Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment

aiRisk.label: AI Risk Assessment
aiRisk.description: General-purpose risk assessment for any AI system. Evaluates operational, ethical, and compliance risks.

conformity.label: Conformity Assessment
conformity.description: Art. 43, Annex VI/VII conformity assessment for high-risk AI systems. Required before market placement.

biasFairness.label: Bias & Fairness Assessment
biasFairness.description: Structured evaluation of bias, fairness metrics, and discrimination risk across protected categories.

assessments.workflowIntro: Every assessment follows a structured approval workflow. Status transitions are logged with timestamps and the acting user for full auditability.
assessments.scoringIntro: Assessments generate risk scores based on question responses. Scores can be manually overridden with justification. The overall risk level determines review requirements and mitigation priorities.

steps.title: Select template
steps.description: Choose from FRIA, AI Risk, Conformity, Bias/Fairness, or Custom templates.

steps.title: Set scope and link AI system
steps.description: Define the assessment scope and link it to the AI system being assessed.

steps.title: Complete questions
steps.description: Answer template questions. The system calculates risk scores as you go.

steps.title: Submit for review

steps.title: Final approval
steps.description: Approved assessments are locked and stored as compliance records.

oversight.metaDescription: Approval gates, review scheduling, and decision logging for EU AI Act Art. 14 compliance.
oversight.title: Human Oversight
oversight.intro: Implement Art. 14 human oversight requirements for high-risk AI systems. Configure approval gates at key lifecycle stages, schedule periodic reviews, and maintain a complete decision log for regulators.
oversight.gateTypesIntro: Oversight gates are checkpoints that require human review and approval before an AI system can proceed. Each gate is linked to a specific AI system and assigned to a reviewer.

gateTypes.description: Required before an AI system moves from Testing to Deployed status. Ensures all compliance requirements are met.
Triggered after deployment to verify the system performs as expected in production. Monitors for unexpected behavior.
Scheduled at regular intervals (e.g., quarterly). Reviews ongoing performance, drift, and continued compliance.
Automatically requested when an AI incident is reported against the system. Requires review before continued operation.
Required when significant changes are made to the AI system (new model, different data sources, expanded scope).

oversight.decisionIntro: Every oversight decision is logged with the reviewer, timestamp, decision outcome, and rationale. This forms the Art. 14 audit trail required for high-risk AI systems.

approve.label: Approve
approve.body: System is cleared to proceed. The reviewer confirms all requirements are satisfied.

reject.label: Reject
reject.body: System is not cleared. The reviewer documents the reasons and required remediation steps.

defer.label: Defer
defer.body: Decision is postponed pending additional information. A follow-up date is set.

steps.title: Navigate to Oversight
steps.description: Go to Governance → Oversight from the top navigation.

steps.title: Create a new gate
steps.description: Click New Oversight Gate. Select the AI system and gate type (pre-deployment, periodic, etc.).

steps.title: Assign a reviewer
steps.description: Select the team member responsible for the review. They will be notified when the gate is triggered.

steps.title: Set the schedule
steps.description: For periodic reviews, configure the review cadence (e.g., quarterly, annually).

steps.title: Conduct the review
steps.description: When the gate is triggered, review the system documentation, evidence, and current status. Log your decision with a rationale.

incidents.metaDescription: Track AI-specific failures, coordinate response tasks, and manage Art. 73 authority notifications.
incidents.title: AI Incidents
incidents.intro: Track AI-specific incidents from initial report through resolution. Manage response timelines, coordinate tasks, and handle Art. 73 authority notifications for serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems.
incidents.typesIntro: AI SENTINEL tracks incident types specific to AI systems, distinct from data protection incidents handled in DPO Central.
incidents.lifecycleIntro: Every incident follows a structured workflow. Status transitions and timestamps are tracked for compliance evidence.
incidents.severityIntro: Severity levels prioritize response efforts and determine notification requirements.

low.description: Minor incident, limited impact. No regulatory notification required.

medium.description: Moderate impact, contained quickly. Internal review recommended.

high.description: Significant impact. Likely requires authority notification under Art. 73.

critical.description: Large-scale failure or safety risk. Immediate Art. 73 notification required.

incidents.art73Intro: Under EU AI Act Article 73, providers of high-risk AI systems must report serious incidents to the relevant market surveillance authority. AI SENTINEL tracks notification deadlines, recipient authorities, and submission status.

art73.whenBody: Serious incidents involving death, serious damage to health, property, or the environment, or serious and irreversible disruption of critical infrastructure.
art73.timelineBody: Report immediately after establishing a causal link (or its reasonable likelihood) and no later than 15 days after awareness — 10 days if the incident involves a death, 2 days for widespread infringements or serious and irreversible disruption of critical infrastructure. The system tracks elapsed time from the incident report date.
art73.includeBody: Description of the incident, affected AI system, severity, root cause analysis (if available), and corrective measures taken or planned.

incidents.timelineIntro: Each incident maintains a detailed timeline recording all events, status changes, task assignments, and communications.

rootCause.event: Root cause identified — model drift detected

reportSteps.title: Report the incident
reportSteps.description: Navigate to Operations → Incidents and click Report Incident. Provide initial details: affected AI system, incident type, and description.

reportSteps.title: Triage and assign severity
reportSteps.description: Review the report, assign a severity level, and determine the response scope.

reportSteps.title: Investigate and contain
reportSteps.description: Gather evidence, identify the root cause, and implement immediate containment measures.

reportSteps.title: Notify authorities if required
reportSteps.description: For high-risk systems with serious incidents, prepare and submit the Art. 73 notification.

reportSteps.title: Resolve and close
reportSteps.description: Document the resolution, lessons learned, and any corrective actions. Close the incident.

transparency.metaDescription: Track EU AI Act Art. 50 transparency obligations per AI system: AI interaction disclosure, synthetic-content marking, emotion recognition, and deepfake labelling.
transparency.title: Transparency (Art. 50)
transparency.intro: Article 50 of the EU AI Act imposes transparency duties that cut across risk tiers: even a minimal-risk chatbot owes a disclosure. AI SENTINEL tracks the four Art. 50 obligations per AI system, splits them by who actually owes them, and counts down the one deadline that has a transitional period.
transparency.applicabilityBody1: Art. 50 has applied since 2 August 2026 (Art. 113). Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 — the Digital Omnibus on AI, OJ L of 24 July 2026 — grants systems placed on the market before that date a transitional period for the machine-readable marking duty in Art. 50(2), running to 2 December 2026.
transparency.applicabilityBody2: That grace period is the reason the AI Registry asks whether a system was placed on the market before 2 August 2026. Answer it accurately: it is the only input that moves the marking deadline, and the dashboard's “marking overdue” counter is derived from it.
transparency.obligationsIntro: Two are owed by the provider and two by the deployer. A single organization often holds both roles, but recording them separately is what lets you answer a regulator asking which hat you were wearing.

obligations.title: AI interaction disclosure
obligations.description: Systems that interact directly with people must make clear they are AI, unless that is obvious to a reasonably well-informed person. Chatbots and voice agents are the typical case.

obligations.title: Machine-readable marking of synthetic content
obligations.description: Systems generating synthetic audio, image, video, or text must mark their output in a machine-readable format detectable as artificially generated. This is the obligation with a transitional deadline — see below.

obligations.title: Emotion recognition and biometric categorisation
obligations.description: Deployers must inform the people exposed to an emotion-recognition or biometric-categorisation system that it is in use. Note that several such uses are prohibited outright under Art. 5 — the module flags that overlap rather than letting you record a disclosure for a practice you cannot lawfully run.

obligations.title: Deepfake and public-interest text labelling
obligations.description: Deployers publishing deepfakes must disclose that the content is artificially generated or manipulated. The same applies to AI-generated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest.

statuses.name: Not applicable
statuses.description: This obligation does not apply to the system. The default for every obligation until you decide otherwise.

statuses.name: Required
statuses.description: The obligation applies and is not yet satisfied. Systems in this state drive the deadline counters on the executive dashboard.

statuses.name: Implemented
statuses.description: The obligation applies and the disclosure or marking is in place. Record how in the AI statement so the evidence survives staff turnover.

workingSteps.body: Every AI system in the registry has a Transparency (Art. 50) tab alongside Models, Data Sources, and Risk Classification.
The module screens the system's purpose and technique and suggests which of the four obligations look applicable. Treat these as prompts, not conclusions — you confirm each one.
Mark each as Not applicable, Required, or Implemented. Anything left Required appears in the dashboard's transparency counters.
Record the disclosure wording and the marking method you actually use. This is the artifact a market surveillance authority will ask for; a status field alone will not satisfy them.

transparency.scopeBody: This module records your Art. 50 position; it does not mark content for you. Machine-readable marking is implemented in the generating system itself. AI SENTINEL is where you document which systems owe the duty, whether it is satisfied, and how — so the answer exists before someone asks for it.

compliance.metaDescription: Framework mapping for EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, and ISO 42001 with evidence management and export.
compliance.title: Compliance
compliance.intro: Map your AI systems against leading regulatory frameworks. Track compliance status at the requirement level, attach evidence, and export compliance packages for regulators and auditors.
compliance.frameworksIntro: AI SENTINEL ships with three pre-loaded frameworks. Each framework is broken down into articles, clauses, or functions with individual compliance tracking.

euAiAct.name: EU AI Act
euAiAct.description: Key-obligation mapping from Art. 4 (AI literacy) and Art. 5 (prohibited practices) through Art. 73 (serious incidents) and the Art. 113 applicability timeline, plus relevant annexes. The primary regulatory framework for AI systems in the European Union.

nist.name: NIST AI RMF
nist.description: The US National Institute of Standards and Technology AI Risk Management Framework. Four core functions with sub-categories.

iso.name: ISO 42001
iso.description: International standard for AI Management Systems. Covers organizational context, leadership, planning, support, and operations.

compliance.statusesIntro: Each requirement can be independently assessed for every AI system. The status reflects the current compliance posture for that specific requirement.
compliance.matrixIntro: The compliance matrix provides a per-AI-system view of all requirements within a chosen framework. For each requirement, you can set the compliance status, add notes, and attach evidence documents.
compliance.crossIntro: Many requirements across the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, and ISO 42001 overlap conceptually. AI SENTINEL includes 41 pre-built cross-framework mappings so that one compliance effort can satisfy requirements across multiple frameworks simultaneously.
compliance.crossBody1: When you mark a requirement as <s>Compliant</s> or <s>Partially Compliant</s>, AI SENTINEL shows linked requirements from other frameworks and offers to propagate the status automatically.
compliance.crossBody2: For example, marking EU AI Act Art. 9 (Risk Management) as compliant can automatically update NIST GOVERN 1 (Risk Management Policies) and ISO 42001 Clause 6.1 (Actions to Address Risks) — because they cover the same obligation.
compliance.snapshotBody1: When you classify an AI system's risk level (e.g., High Risk under the EU AI Act), AI SENTINEL automatically creates compliance mapping records for every applicable requirement across all three frameworks. You arrive at the compliance matrix with all relevant controls pre-populated — no manual setup needed.
compliance.snapshotBody2: For a High Risk system, this means 80+ requirements are instantly initialized across EU AI Act (Art. 6 through Art. 73 key requirements), NIST AI RMF (all 23 practices), and ISO 42001 clauses, each set to “Not Assessed” and ready for evaluation.

steps.title: Navigate to Compliance
steps.description: Go to Governance → Compliance from the top navigation.

steps.title: Select framework and AI system
steps.description: Choose the framework (EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, or ISO 42001) and the AI system to assess.

steps.title: Assess each requirement
steps.description: Work through the requirements list. For each, set the compliance status and add notes or evidence.

steps.title: Filter by applicability
steps.description: Use risk-level filtering to focus on requirements that apply to your system's classification (e.g., high-risk only).

steps.title: Export documentation
steps.description: Generate CSV or PDF reports for regulatory submissions, audits, or internal stakeholders.

vendors.metaDescription: Third-party AI vendor management with risk assessment, contract tracking, and due diligence.
vendors.title: Vendor Risk
vendors.intro: Manage third-party AI vendors with risk assessment, contract lifecycle tracking, and due diligence documentation. Maintain a complete registry of every AI vendor your organization relies on.
vendors.riskIntro: Each vendor is assigned a risk level based on the criticality of the AI services they provide. Risk level determines review frequency and due diligence requirements.
vendors.statusIntro: Vendors progress through a review and approval workflow before being cleared for use.
vendors.recordIntro: Each vendor record captures the information needed for risk management and contract oversight.
vendors.catalogIntro: The AI Vendor Catalog (powered by Vendor.Watch) provides a pre-audited database of AI vendors. Search the catalog, view vendor profiles, and add vendors directly to your registry with auto-filled details.
vendors.catalogSearchBody: Search by vendor name or browse by category. Each catalog entry includes a description, website, and compliance flags.
vendors.catalogAutofillBody: When adding a vendor from the catalog, the form is auto-filled with the vendor's details — saving time and ensuring accuracy.
vendors.catalogRegisterBody: Optionally register the vendor's product as an AI system in your registry at the same time, linking the vendor and system records.

steps.title: Navigate to Vendors
steps.description: Go to Operations → Vendors from the top navigation.

steps.title: Click Add Vendor
steps.description: Use the button in the top-right corner. Optionally search the AI Vendor Catalog to auto-fill details.

steps.title: Complete vendor details
steps.description: Enter the vendor name, website, contact, services, and assign a risk level.

steps.title: Add contract information
steps.description: Document contract dates, renewal terms, and SLA details.

steps.title: Schedule risk assessments
steps.description: From the vendor detail page, create vendor risk assessments and set review schedules.

policies.metaDescription: AI governance policies with versioning, approval workflow, and system linking.
policies.title: Policy Management
policies.intro: Author, version, and manage AI governance policies. Link policies to specific AI systems, track approval workflows, and maintain a living policy library that evolves with your organization.
policies.typesIntro: AI SENTINEL supports a range of policy types covering the full scope of AI governance. Each type addresses a specific governance domain.

types.description: Rules for how AI systems may be used within the organization
Overarching governance structure, roles, and responsibilities
Ethical principles and guidelines for AI development and deployment
Risk identification, assessment, and mitigation procedures
Data quality, provenance, and handling requirements for AI
Standards for evaluating and acquiring AI systems and services
Procedures for responding to AI-related incidents
Disclosure and explainability requirements for AI decisions
User-defined policy type for organization-specific needs

policies.workflowIntro: Policies follow a structured lifecycle from drafting through publication. Each stage transition is logged for audit purposes.
policies.versionsIntro: Every content change to a policy creates a new version. The system automatically tracks the version number, change notes, author, and timestamp. Previous versions remain accessible for comparison.
versionNotes: Updated transparency requirements for generative AI systems
Added procurement guidelines for third-party AI vendors
Initial policy draft covering AI usage rules
policies.linkingIntro: Policies can be linked to specific AI systems in the registry. This creates traceability between governance policies and the systems they apply to, making it easy to see which policies govern a particular AI system.
policies.linkingFromPolicyBody: View and manage which AI systems are covered by the policy. Add or remove system links from the policy detail page.
policies.linkingFromSystemBody: View all policies that apply to a specific AI system. This helps AI officers understand the full governance context.

steps.title: Navigate to Policies
steps.description: Go to Governance → Policies from the top navigation.

steps.title: Click New Policy
steps.description: Choose the policy type and enter a title and description.

steps.title: Author the content
steps.description: Write the policy content. Each save creates a new version automatically.

steps.title: Link AI systems
steps.description: Associate the policy with the AI systems it applies to.

steps.title: Submit for review
steps.description: Change the status to Under Review. Approvers will review and either approve or request changes.

steps.title: Publish
steps.description: Once approved, publish the policy to make it visible organization-wide. Set an effective date and review schedule.

shadowAi.metaTitle: Shadow AI Discovery — AI SENTINEL Docs
shadowAi.metaDescription: Discover unauthorized AI tools in your organization. Self-reporting portal, triage workflow, and promotion to formal governance.
shadowAi.title: Shadow AI Discovery
shadowAi.intro: Shadow AI refers to AI tools adopted by employees without the knowledge or approval of the organization. Research suggests that around 60% of employees use unapproved AI tools at work — from ChatGPT and Copilot to image generators and AI-powered analytics. Organizations cannot govern AI systems they do not know about.
shadowAi.whatP1: Shadow AI is the AI equivalent of Shadow IT — the use of AI-powered tools, services, and applications by employees without explicit organizational authorization. Unlike formally procured vendors that go through risk assessment and contract review, shadow AI tools enter the organization through individual adoption: an engineer installs a code assistant, a lawyer uses ChatGPT for contract review, a marketing team signs up for an AI copywriting tool.
shadowAi.whatP2: Under the EU AI Act, organizations that deploy AI systems have specific obligations as deployers — regardless of whether the deployment was sanctioned or not. Shadow AI creates blind spots in compliance, data protection, and risk management programs.

whyItems.title: Compliance risk
whyItems.description: Unregistered AI systems may fall under high-risk categories without appropriate conformity assessments, human oversight, or risk documentation.

whyItems.title: Data protection
whyItems.description: Employees may input personal data, trade secrets, or client information into AI tools that train on user inputs or store data in non-compliant jurisdictions.

whyItems.title: Regulatory exposure
whyItems.description: Under the EU AI Act, deployers are responsible for AI systems used within their organization — even those adopted informally by staff.

whyItems.title: Governance gap
whyItems.description: You cannot classify risk, run assessments, or set oversight gates for AI systems you do not know exist. Shadow AI is the missing first step.

shadowAi.vsIntro: Shadow AI Discovery and Vendor Risk Management solve fundamentally different problems in opposite directions. They are complementary, not overlapping.
vsVendorItems: Organization procures a vendor through formal channels
Known from day one — the org chose the vendor
Core question: “Is this vendor we selected risky?”
vsShadowItems: Employees adopt AI tools on their own, outside procurement
Core question: “What AI tools are people actually using?”
Lifecycle: Discovery → Triage → Approve or Prohibit

howSteps.title: Employees self-report
howSteps.description: Staff search a pre-loaded catalog of 36 known AI tools across 8 categories (LLM Chat, Code Assistants, Image Generation, Video/Audio, Writing, Business Tools, Data Analytics, Search) or enter a custom tool. They specify their department, usage description, and how they use the tool.

howSteps.title: Triage and review
howSteps.description: Reported tools enter the review queue with status DISCOVERED. The AI Officer or governance team reviews each tool, assessing risk indicators: Does it process personal data? Does it train on input? Is it cloud-hosted? SOC2 certified? GDPR compliant?

howSteps.title: Approve or prohibit
howSteps.description: Each tool is either APPROVED for continued use (with conditions) or PROHIBITED and flagged for removal. Prohibited tools trigger a clear organizational signal that the tool is not sanctioned.

howSteps.title: Promote to formal governance
howSteps.description: Approved shadow tools can be promoted into the AI Registry as a formal AI System — and optionally into a Vendor record — in a single step. This bridges informal discovery into your full governance program.

vendorCatalog.metaTitle: AI Vendor Catalog — AI SENTINEL Docs
vendorCatalog.metaDescription: Pre-audited catalog of 665+ AI vendors with risk profiles, compliance data, and governance metadata powered by Vendor.Watch.
vendorCatalog.title: AI Vendor Catalog
vendorCatalog.intro: Evaluating AI vendors from scratch is time-consuming and error-prone. The AI Vendor Catalog gives your governance team a head start with pre-audited profiles for 665+ AI vendors — complete with risk indicators, compliance certifications, and deployment metadata.
vendorCatalog.whatTitle: What is the AI Vendor Catalog?
vendorCatalog.whatP1: The AI Vendor Catalog is a searchable, pre-populated directory of AI tool and service providers. Each vendor profile includes structured governance data: what the vendor does, where data is processed, what certifications they hold, whether they train on customer data, and their EU AI Act risk classification.
vendorCatalog.whatP2: The catalog is powered by <vw>Vendor.Watch</vw>, an independent AI vendor intelligence service that continuously audits and updates vendor profiles. Data syncs automatically, so your catalog stays current without manual research.

whyItems.title: Due diligence at scale
whyItems.description: Manually researching each AI vendor's data practices, certifications, and risk posture is impractical. The catalog provides a standardized baseline for every vendor evaluation.

whyItems.title: Faster procurement
whyItems.description: When a team requests a new AI tool, governance can check the catalog immediately — no weeks-long vendor questionnaire cycle needed for initial assessment.

whyItems.title: Regulatory compliance
whyItems.description: The EU AI Act requires deployers to understand the AI systems they use. Pre-classified vendor risk levels and compliance indicators help meet Art. 6 and Art. 26 obligations.

whyItems.title: Continuous updates
whyItems.description: Vendor risk profiles change as companies update their terms, certifications expire, or data practices evolve. Automated sync ensures your catalog reflects current reality.

vendorCatalog.vsIntro: The AI Vendor Catalog and the Vendor Risk module serve different purposes in the governance lifecycle. They complement each other.
vsCatalogItems: Read-only reference for initial due diligence
Core question: “What do we know about this vendor?”
vsRiskItems: Internal assessments — your team's risk evaluations
Full CRUD with status tracking and contract management
Core question: “How risky is this vendor for us?”

profileItems.fields: Name, slug, logo, website, description, category, headquarters country
Model names, model types (proprietary, open-source, fine-tuned), training data transparency
Data processing locations, data retention policy, trains on customer data (yes/no), sub-processors disclosed
SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR compliance status, EU AI Act risk classification, HIPAA eligibility
Last audit date, Vendor.Watch risk score, catalog sync timestamp, source URL

howSteps.title: Browse or search
howSteps.description: Search the catalog by vendor name, category, or compliance attribute. Filter by risk level, certification status, or data processing location.

howSteps.title: Review the profile
howSteps.description: Each vendor has a detailed profile page with structured governance data — risk indicators, compliance certifications, data practices, and AI model information.

howSteps.title: Inform your decision
howSteps.description: Use the catalog data to accelerate vendor assessments, support procurement decisions, or evaluate shadow AI tools that employees have reported.

howSteps.title: Automatic sync
howSteps.description: The catalog syncs with Vendor.Watch on a regular schedule. New vendors are added and existing profiles are updated automatically as intelligence becomes available.

conformity.metaDescription: EU AI Act Art. 43 conformity assessment template for high-risk AI systems. Structured evaluation of technical documentation, quality management, and post-market monitoring.
conformity.title: Conformity Assessment
conformity.intro: High-risk AI systems under the EU AI Act must undergo a conformity assessment before being placed on the market. AI SENTINEL provides a structured template that walks your team through every requirement — from technical documentation to post-market monitoring — so nothing falls through the cracks.
conformity.whatP1: A conformity assessment is a formal evaluation process required by Art. 43 of the EU AI Act for high-risk AI systems. It verifies that the AI system meets all applicable requirements before deployment — covering data governance, transparency, human oversight, accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity.
conformity.whatP2: Depending on the use case, conformity assessments may be conducted internally by the provider or through a third-party notified body. In either case, the assessment must follow a structured methodology and produce documented evidence of compliance.

whoItems.title: AI Providers
whoItems.description: Organizations that develop or place high-risk AI systems on the EU market must complete a conformity assessment before deployment (Art. 16).

whoItems.title: AI Deployers
whoItems.description: Organizations deploying high-risk AI systems must verify that the provider has completed the conformity assessment and that the CE marking is in place (Art. 26).

whoItems.title: Annex III systems
whoItems.description: AI systems used in biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, employment, essential services, law enforcement, migration, or administration of justice (Art. 6(2)).

whoItems.title: Internal compliance teams
whoItems.description: Even when a notified body is involved, internal teams need a structured process to prepare documentation, gather evidence, and track remediation of gaps.

coversItems.description: Verification that a risk management system is established and maintained throughout the AI system lifecycle (Art. 9).
Assessment of training, validation, and testing data — including relevance, representativeness, and bias examination (Art. 10).
Review of technical documentation completeness: system description, design specifications, development process, and performance metrics (Art. 11, Annex IV).
Evaluation of automatic logging capabilities for traceability, including input/output records and system events (Art. 12).
Assessment of instructions for use, disclosure of AI nature, and interpretability measures for deployers and affected persons (Art. 13).
Verification that appropriate human oversight measures are designed into the system and documented (Art. 14).
Testing and validation of accuracy levels, resilience to errors and adversarial attacks, and cybersecurity measures (Art. 15).
Review of the provider's quality management system covering development processes, testing, and post-market obligations (Art. 17).
Verification that a post-market monitoring plan is in place to detect and address issues after deployment (Art. 72).

howSteps.title: Create a new assessment
howSteps.description: Select the Conformity Assessment template and link it to a registered AI system. The template pre-populates all required evaluation areas.

howSteps.title: Work through each section
howSteps.description: Each section presents structured questions aligned to the EU AI Act requirements. Record findings, attach evidence, and note any gaps.

howSteps.title: Submit for review
howSteps.description: Once complete, submit the assessment for review by the AI Officer or governance lead. The approval workflow tracks sign-off and any requested changes.

howSteps.title: Document and maintain
howSteps.description: The completed assessment becomes part of your compliance record. Link it to the AI system's compliance mapping and revisit it when material changes occur.

biasFairness.metaTitle: Bias & Fairness Assessment — AI SENTINEL Docs
biasFairness.metaDescription: Structured bias and fairness evaluation for AI systems. Detect discrimination risks, assess protected attributes, and document mitigation measures.
biasFairness.title: Bias & Fairness Assessment
biasFairness.intro: AI systems can produce discriminatory outcomes — often unintentionally. The Bias & Fairness Assessment provides a structured methodology to evaluate your AI systems for bias risks, document affected protected attributes, and track mitigation measures.
biasFairness.whatTitle: What is a Bias & Fairness Assessment?
biasFairness.whatP1: A bias and fairness assessment is a systematic evaluation of an AI system's potential to produce outcomes that unfairly disadvantage individuals or groups based on protected characteristics — such as race, gender, age, disability, ethnicity, or socioeconomic status.
biasFairness.whatP2: Under the EU AI Act, providers of high-risk AI systems must examine training data for possible biases (Art. 10) and implement measures to prevent discriminatory outcomes. The EU Charter of Fundamental Rights (Art. 21) explicitly prohibits discrimination, and AI systems that score, rank, or make decisions about people are particularly exposed to this risk.

whyItems.title: Legal obligation
whyItems.description: The EU AI Act requires bias examination of training data (Art. 10(2)(f)) and non-discrimination safeguards for high-risk systems. Failure to comply carries fines up to 3% of global turnover.

whyItems.title: Fundamental rights
whyItems.description: AI-driven discrimination can violate the right to non-discrimination (EU Charter Art. 21), equal treatment directives, and national equality legislation.

whyItems.title: Real-world impact
whyItems.description: Biased AI in hiring, credit scoring, healthcare triage, or law enforcement has documented consequences — rejected applicants, denied loans, missed diagnoses, and wrongful arrests.

whyItems.title: Reputational risk
whyItems.description: Public disclosure of biased AI outcomes causes lasting reputational damage. Proactive assessment demonstrates responsible AI governance to regulators, customers, and the public.

typesItems.description: Historical data reflects past discrimination. A hiring model trained on historical decisions inherits biases in who was previously hired or promoted.
The training dataset does not represent the population the system will serve. Underrepresented groups receive less accurate predictions.
The features or labels used as proxies are themselves biased. Using zip codes as a feature can encode racial segregation patterns.
A single model is applied to groups with different underlying distributions. Medical AI trained primarily on one demographic may underperform for others.
The system is used in a context different from the one it was designed for, or its outputs are interpreted in a biased manner by human operators.

coversItems.description: Identification of which protected characteristics (age, gender, race, disability, etc.) are relevant to the AI system's domain and affected population.
Evaluation of whether training and testing data adequately represents all relevant groups, including historically underrepresented populations.
Selection and application of appropriate fairness metrics: demographic parity, equalized odds, predictive parity, or individual fairness measures.
Analysis of whether ostensibly neutral features (location, language, education) serve as proxies for protected attributes.
Documentation of pre-processing, in-processing, or post-processing techniques used to reduce identified bias.
Ongoing monitoring strategy to detect bias drift after deployment, including thresholds and escalation procedures.

howSteps.title: Create a new assessment
howSteps.description: Select the Bias & Fairness template and link it to a registered AI system. The template structures the evaluation around the system's specific use case and affected population.

howSteps.title: Evaluate each dimension
howSteps.description: Work through the structured sections: identify relevant protected attributes, assess data representativeness, apply fairness metrics, and check for proxy variables.

howSteps.title: Document findings and mitigations
howSteps.description: Record identified bias risks with severity ratings. For each risk, document the mitigation approach — whether technical (algorithmic debiasing) or procedural (human review).

howSteps.title: Review and monitor
howSteps.description: Submit for approval, then establish ongoing monitoring. The assessment links to your AI system's record so bias findings inform risk classification and oversight decisions.

roles.metaDescription: Understand the five user roles in AI SENTINEL and what each role can do across all governance modules.
roles.title: Roles & Permissions
roles.intro: AI SENTINEL uses five roles to control access to governance operations. Every action is enforced at the server level — the interface adapts to show only what your role allows.

owner.name: Owner
owner.summary: Full platform control. Billing, team management, and all governance operations.

admin.name: Admin
admin.summary: Organization management and full governance access without billing control.

aiOfficer.name: AI Officer
aiOfficer.summary: Governance authority. Approves assessments, publishes policies, and makes oversight decisions.

member.name: Member
member.summary: Day-to-day governance work. Creates records, submits assessments, reports incidents.

viewer.name: Viewer
viewer.summary: Read-only access. Can view all dashboards, records, and reports but cannot make changes.

roles.hierarchyNote: Each role inherits all capabilities from the roles below it.

assign.creatorBody: The user who creates an organization is automatically assigned the <role>Owner</role> role.
assign.invitedBody: Users who are invited or who join via email domain matching receive the <role>Member</role> role by default. An Owner can change their role at any time.
assign.viewerBody: The Viewer role is assigned explicitly by an Owner or Admin. Viewers see a clean read-only interface — create and edit buttons are hidden, not just disabled.
assign.changesBody: Only the organization Owner can change member roles. All role changes are recorded in the audit trail.

roles.enforcementBody: All permissions are enforced at the API level, not just the interface. Even if a user crafts a direct API request, the server verifies their role and organization membership before processing any operation. This means security does not depend on what the browser shows or hides.

security.metaDescription: How AI SENTINEL protects your organization's data with enterprise-grade security controls.
security.title: Security & Trust
security.intro: AI SENTINEL is built for organizations that manage sensitive AI governance data. Security is embedded in every layer of the platform — from how we isolate your data to how we control access and protect your information.

isolation.title: Data Isolation
isolation.intro: Every organization on AI SENTINEL operates in a fully isolated environment. Your AI systems, assessments, policies, incidents, and vendor data are never accessible to other organizations.

items.title: Organization-Scoped Queries
items.description: Every database query is automatically scoped to your organization. There is no way to access another organization's data through the application.

items.title: Verified Membership
items.description: Before any operation, we verify that the requesting user is an active member of the organization. Membership is checked on every single request.

items.title: Cross-Tenant Protection
items.description: Operations that reference related entities (e.g., linking a policy to an AI system) verify that both entities belong to your organization.

items.title: Shared Reference Data Only
items.description: Only non-sensitive reference data (compliance frameworks, assessment templates) is shared across organizations. Your governance data is never shared.

accessControl.title: Access Control
accessControl.intro: AI SENTINEL enforces role-based access control (RBAC) across the entire platform. Every action is checked against your role before it is executed.
accessControl.readOnlyBody: Viewers have guaranteed read-only access. All write operations are blocked at the server level, not just the UI — preventing unauthorized modifications even through API calls.
accessControl.elevatedBody: Sensitive operations like approving assessments, publishing policies, and making oversight decisions require AI Officer, Admin, or Owner roles.

auth.title: Authentication
auth.intro: We support industry-standard authentication methods with additional hardening for production environments.

methods.title: Google OAuth
methods.description: Enterprise SSO via Google with OAuth 2.0

methods.title: Magic Link
methods.description: Passwordless email authentication for secure sign-in

methods.title: Cross-Platform SSO
methods.description: Single sign-on across the TODO.LAW platform

sessionItems: HTTP-only cookies prevent client-side access to session tokens
Secure cookie flag enforced in production (HTTPS only)
CSRF protection on all authenticated requests
SameSite cookie policy prevents cross-site request forgery

validation.title: Input Validation
validation.intro: All user inputs are validated on the server before reaching business logic. This protects against injection attacks and ensures data integrity.

items.title: Schema Validation
items.description: Every API input is validated against a strict schema. Invalid data is rejected before it reaches the database.

items.title: Parameterized Queries
items.description: All database queries use parameterized inputs. Raw SQL is never used, eliminating SQL injection risk.

items.title: Enum Enforcement
items.description: Status fields, risk levels, and categories use strict enum validation. Only predefined values are accepted.

audit.title: Audit Trail
audit.intro: Every create, update, delete, and significant business operation is logged to an immutable audit trail. This supports compliance requirements and provides a complete record of governance activities.
audit.retentionBody: Audit records are preserved even if the associated user or organization is deleted. This ensures your compliance history remains intact regardless of personnel changes.

transport.title: Transport & Infrastructure
transport.intro: Your data is protected in transit and at rest through industry-standard security measures.

items.title: HTTPS Everywhere
items.description: All connections are encrypted with TLS. HSTS headers ensure browsers always use secure connections.

items.title: Clickjacking Protection
items.description: Security headers prevent the application from being embedded in frames on other sites.

items.title: Content Security
items.description: MIME-type sniffing prevention and strict referrer policies protect against content-based attacks.

items.title: Minimal Permissions
items.description: Browser APIs (camera, microphone, geolocation) are explicitly disabled — the application never requests unnecessary access.

api.title: API Security
api.intro: All API endpoints require authentication. External integrations use signature verification and token-based authentication.
api.endpointBody: Every governance API endpoint requires an authenticated session with verified organization membership. Unauthenticated requests are rejected.
api.webhookBody: Payment and integration webhooks use cryptographic signature verification. Unverified webhooks are discarded before processing.

standards.title: Security Standards
standards.intro: AI SENTINEL's security controls are designed to address the OWASP Top 10 web application security risks.

items.description: Parameterized queries, strict input validation, no raw SQL
Industry-standard OAuth, secure sessions, CSRF protection
Comprehensive audit trail for all governance operations

contact.title: Security Contact
contact.body: If you discover a security vulnerability or have questions about our security practices, please contact us at <link>{email}</link>. We take all reports seriously and will respond promptly.
